plang/programming-fundamentals/1-1-terms.comment: The document provides a remarkably clean and frictionless entry point into essential software concepts, using well-structured comparison tables and a clear pipeline flow. Crucial core principles like why assembly serves as an intermediate compiler target and the compile-time vs. runtime safety trade-offs are articulated effectively. However, as an introductory primer, it stays at a high conceptual level without diving into lower-level architectural mechanics or execution binaries.

plang/programming-fundamentals/1-2-class.comment: The text systematically categorizes programming languages across three core axes while clearly distinguishing non-programming markup and query languages. It excels in structural readability and intuitive pedagogical flow, effectively explaining the underlying mechanics behind execution models and paradigms. To achieve theoretical mastery, it could further incorporate concrete mathematical models or deep execution traces of dynamic translation.

plang/programming-fundamentals/1-3-code-.comment: The document effectively connects basic code primitives to underlying compiler mechanics such as lexical analysis, AST creation, and runtime execution contexts. It balances foundational accessibility with technical precision by systematically clarifying the role of syntax, static/dynamic semantics, and language execution models. Incorporating explicit visual AST nodes or binary level entry point details would further deepen its conceptual rigor.

plang/programming-fundamentals/2-1-varia.comment: The manuscript offers a clean and intuitively structured overview of variables, constants, and literals, making it accessible for beginners. However, it lacks deep first-principles analysis regarding lower-level memory mechanics, compiler handling of static literals, and underlying computer architecture.
